snippet.title: Cameron Purdy: Designing the XVM: the Ecstasy Virtual Machine
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #jfokus #java #foss



The XVM is a new managed runtime design, synthesizing ideas from a variety of languages and runtimes to achieve provable security, deep monitorability, and real time resource management capability. This presentation will look at the design of the portable executable format, the intermediate representation (IR) for compiled code, the threading model, and the memory model.


Cameron Purdy, xtclang.org
@cpurdy
Cameron Purdy is an 11x developer, co-creator of the Ecstasy programming language, and co-author of Oracle Coherence. Cameron is co-founder and CEO of xqiz.it. Previously, he was co-founder and CEO of Tangosol, acquired by Oracle, where he was the Senior Vice President for enterprise Java, WebLogic, Coherence, Traffic Director, and Exalogic products. Cameron is a contributor to the Java Language and Virtual Machine specifications, author of the Portable Object Format (POF) specification, and author of a plethora of patents on distributed computing and data management.

snippet.title: Tobias Tebbi: V8 Torque: A Typed Language to Implement JavaScript
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #jfokus #V8 #javascript

When implementing a language VM, there are a number of choices on how to implement the runtime and standard library. For the V8 JavaScript engine, we have tried many different approaches over the years: handwritten assembly, C++, self-hosted (i.e., using JavaScript) and more. With V8 Torque, we now have our own domain-specific language to write JavaScript built-in functionality in a statically typed language compatible with our runtime and garbage collector. This enables better productivity by having maintainable code, better security by static checking, and seamless inter-op with the rest of the system. With V8 Torque, we expose VM internals while hiding and enforcing invariants and assumptions.

Tobias Tebbi, Google
Tobias is a software engineer at Google Munich. As part of the V8 team, he works on V8 Torque, a domain-specific language for the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine that exposes VM internals in a safe and performant way.

snippet.title: Robbin Ehn: Handshaking HotSpot
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #jfokus #java #foss

The HotSpot JVM has relied on global safepoints for accessing thread local resources safely. Recently a thread local poll mechanism was added. This lets the JVM target individual threads and removes inter-thread dependencies. The per-thread operation - the handshake - can be executed directly when the target thread is in a safe state. This helps reduce application latency and throughput.

We take a deeper look into the handshake implementation, outline current uses such as ZGC, deoptimization and lock revocation and peek into future applications.

Robbin EhnOracle
Robbin Ehn is a member of the Oracle HotSpot runtime team, working mainly on concurrency, locking and safepointing. With a background in telecommunications and high frequency trading he joined Oracle in 2016.

snippet.title: Dan Heidinga: Project Valhalla: Bringing Values to Java
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #java #jfokus #foss

Project Valhalla has been in development for over 5 years now. What can be so hard about bringing value types to Java? Come to this session to learn from someone who's been involved in this project since it's beginning about what value types are, how they're implemented, and how your applications will benefit from their increased memory density and lack of identity.

Dan Heidinga, @DanHeidinga, IBM
Dan Heidinga is an Eclipse OpenJ9 project lead while also leading IBM's J9 VM Interpreter team. He has been involved with virtual machine development since 2007 and has represented IBM on multple JSRS include JSR 292 ('invokedynamic') and JSR 335 ('lambda'). He has his hands in most new JVM features and all major Java releases. In the past he's spent entirely too long staring at Java bytecode while maintaining the verifier and still enjoys an occasional detour into Smalltalk development.

snippet.title: Claes Redestad: Heap Archiving
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #jfokus #java #foss

Heap Archiving

Since JDK 12, there is a general purpose facility to store closed and open-ended heap graphs into CDS archives. This means we have a few new tricks we can pull to avoid work done during startup while reducing footprint.

In this talk I'll look at the current implementation, how it works, what initialization we have already done away with and how we'll do away with even more. I'll contrast it with related features, including condy, the constants API, lazy finals.

Time allowing, we'll also look at the grand plan of storing lambdas and other dynamically generated classes into CDS archives - or why not doing it at jlink time, ultimately making it all available to closed-world AOT compilers?

Claes Redestad, Oracle, @cl4es
Claes has been working as an OpenJDK performance engineer at Oracle since 2012, benchmarking, developing and improving the runtime in many ways small and large ever since. Living in Stockholm, Sweden, Claes enjoys good coffee, bad puns and rugby.

snippet.title: Charlie Gracie: Current state of JVM Escape Analysis and downstream optimizations
snippet.description:
Jfokus VM Tech Summit 2020 https://www.jfokus.se/vmtech #java #jfokus #foss

What is escape analysis (EA) and how is it used to optimize JVM workloads? I would like to share my results of analyzing EA and the effect downstream optimizations have on heap pressure. What is scalar replacement of objects? How is it different from stack allocation? I will discuss how C2, Graal and OpenJ9 use data from EA to perform different optimizations. Can the OpenJDK community improve C2 to provide a more efficient JVM by improving the post EA optimizations?

Charlie Gracie, Microsoft, @crgracie
Charlie Gracie is a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft and he has been involved in virtual machine development for more than 15 years. The majority of his runtime experience is in Garbage Collection and multi threaded scalability. His passion is improving the performance of runtimes and the applications running on them. He is also a Project Lead on the Eclipse OMR project.
